title: Palantir WEF identity resolution and headquarters-source staleness
summary: Primary WEF and SEC evidence bridges WEF's Palantir Technologies display name to Palantir Technologies Inc.; WEF's Denver headquarters text conflicts with newer company and SEC principal-executive-office evidence for Aventura, Florida.

sources.title: Palantir Technologies Inc. Form 10-Q for period ended 2026-03-31
World Economic Forum Annual Meeting 2026 partners

provenance.method: primary-source entity resolution and location-source freshness review

data.question: Do the WEF-facing Palantir Technologies record and legal issuer Palantir Technologies Inc. represent the same organization, and which headquarters/location evidence is current?
data.method: Compared current WEF organization, WEF executive, WEF partner, SEC issuer, and existing first-party principal-office evidence.
data.framework: Exact-name, executive-role, issuer-identifier, first-party website, and temporal source-semantics reconciliation.
data.scope: Public organizational identity and organizational location only.
findings: WEF's Alex Karp profile explicitly names Palantir Technologies Inc., bridging WEF's Palantir Technologies display-name surface to the SEC legal issuer.
SEC identifies Palantir Technologies Inc. as CIK 0001321655 and reports 19505 Biscayne Boulevard, Suite 2350, Aventura, Florida 33180 as business and mailing address.

WEF's current Palantir organization profile still describes Denver, Colorado as headquarters, making that profile location text stale or semantically divergent relative to newer company and regulatory principal-executive-office evidence.
conclusions: The two normalized Palantir organization IDs represent the same operating/legal organization at high confidence; canonical consolidation should preserve WEF provenance and use the legal issuer identity as the canonical anchor.
For current organizational location, newer Palantir/SEC principal-executive-office evidence should outrank WEF's older Denver profile text without pretending the two source semantics are identical.
recommendations: Perform canonical ID rewiring only through the repository's scripted normalized-DB write/import path.
Monitor WEF's Palantir profile for an explicit headquarters update.
counterarguments: WEF may use headquarters as an editorial profile field with a slower refresh cadence than SEC principal-executive-office reporting.
limitations: This pass does not infer that principal executive office is legally identical to every use of headquarters.
No private locations or coordinates were collected.
unresolved: When will WEF update the Denver headquarters text, and what exact headquarters wording will it use after refresh?
